question: Can Craft Anything rebuild an app?

points.claim: Craft Anything studies the original with real inspection tools before any AI builds.
points.spoken: It studies the original first, with real inspection tools, before any AI writes a line.
points.source_note: README 'How it works', step 1: Study: inspect the original: its pages at every width, its code, its files, how it runs.

visual.intent: study stage, as the README lists it: three steps lit as they are said

points.title: Study before it builds
points.sub: It inspects the original first, using real tools, not guesses.

points.claim: A coding agent then builds a new project in the stack you ask for.
points.spoken: Then a coding agent builds a new project, in the language or framework you ask for.
points.source_note: README 'How it works', step 2: Build: a coding agent builds a new project, in the language, framework or engine your request names.

visual.intent: build stage: name the stack, the agent builds, then check and refine

points.title: Then an agent builds
points.sub: You name the stack, and the agent builds the new project in it.

points.claim: Each build is checked against the original at three screen widths, and differences are listed.
points.spoken: Every build is checked against the original, at three screen widths, and mismatches are listed.
points.source_note: README feature table: Checked, not guessed: pages at three screen widths; refined until it's close.

points.title: Checked, not guessed

points.claim: Every tool is both a command line call and an MCP tool, so an agent can drive the same engine.
points.spoken: Every tool is a command line call and an MCP tool, so an agent can drive the same engine the app uses.
points.source_note: README feature table: 320 tools, each one a CLI command and an MCP tool; no AI is needed to inspect.

visual.intent: the two ways an agent reaches the same engine

points.title: Agents drive the same engine
